name: sim_bench
description: How fast the simulation steps natively at a busy moment (design 6.8, M4): four seats (two Lamplighters, two Lookouts, played by the caretaker from tick 0) at wave 11 of High Water, loaded from the checkpoint at its horn and stepped through 1,800 ticks, the longest catch-up, with events drained every tick. Reports native ticks per second (best of three runs) and fails below the floor in tests/sim/sim_bench.gd, set from the first measurement (about 4,300 to 5,200 with M3's scan of every creep, 12,000 to 15,000 with the look along the road; the floor of 4,000 leaves room for a CI runner). The load is the caretaker's: 27 towers at wave 11's horn, about half of the 59 that four players spending their gold stood in the M4 review's probes (design 6.7's '60 towers'), so the rate here reads about twice a four-player board's (the review measured 12,632 against 6,826 ticks a second on one machine). The floor cannot tell a tick that lost the walk along the road (the scan alone steps about 4,100 to 4,300 here), so the bench also counts the ticks whose own stage 5 sorted the creeps (SimMatch.walks, in measure()) and fails unless nearly all did. On the same ticks it times stage 5's walk along the road against the scan it replaced and fails unless the walk is at least three times faster (about 8.7 measured), which holds on any machine. Each run reaches the same state hash. A timing, so --determinism leaves it out. Measured with the four M4 tracks merged (the measured key): 15,779 native ticks a second, the walk 8.5 times faster than the scan, a 2,583-byte checkpoint at the end and 3,866 bytes the largest at any hash tick on the way (measured after the M4 review), well under the design's 10 KB.

measured.where: the 16-thread Linux laptop the floor was set on, headless, sim_bench alone, three runs
measured.web_export: not measured yet (design 6.8's 2,000 ticks a second, by hand)

steps.msg: four seats reached wave 11's horn with their towers standing

steps.eval: print('SIM_BENCH native ticks_per_second=%d runs=%s creeps<=%d shots<=%d checkpoint_bytes=%d largest_checkpoint_bytes=%d look_walk_us=%d look_scan_us=%d look_speedup_pc=%d walk_ticks=%d' % [bench['ticks_per_second'], str(bench['runs']), bench['most_creeps'], bench['most_shots'], bench['checkpoint_bytes'], bench['largest_checkpoint_bytes'], look['walk_us'], look['scan_us'], look['speedup_pc'], bench['walk_ticks']])
